SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch. Shanghai.
REPORT
Date February 9, 1935.

Subject (in full) Ban on "Hula Hula Dance," the song "Dau Hua Kiang" and the
drama "Ba Sz Doong" by Bureau of Education.

Made by D.I. Everest    Forwarded by 〔此处转录不清〕

Further efforts on the part of the Chinese staff of this
Section to locate any Chinese place of entertainment in the
Settlement where the Chinese song "Dau Hua Kiang" and the
drama "Ba Sz Doong" are surreptitiously rendered have been
unsuccessful.

D. I.

Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch).

S3,
Please note with a view to reporting
any cases of this character which
come to your notice and pass to
Reg. Office.
〔此处转录不清〕
〔签名〕
11.2.35

File No. S. B. REGISTRY.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
特务科第二股。上海。
报告
日期：1935年2月9日。

主题（全称）教育局禁止“胡拉胡拉舞”、歌曲《Dau Hua Kiang》及
戏剧《Ba Sz Doong》。

由警督 Everest 呈报    转呈者〔此处转录不清〕

本科华籍职员为查找租界内任何暗中表演中文歌曲
《Dau Hua Kiang》及戏剧《Ba Sz Doong》的华人娱乐场所，
已进一步做出努力，但未获成功。

副总监（特务科）。

S3，
请注意，以便向
注册办公室通报
你方获悉的此类案件。
〔此处转录不清〕
〔签名〕
1935年2月11日

Station,
REPORT
Date January ____ 1938.

Subject: In regard to "Haa Haa Dance," the song "Daa Haa Kiang" and
the drama "Ba Se Dong," by Bureau of Education.

Made by D. __________ Forwarded by J.B.Rn S.

Reference the entertainment notes "A" in the attached
report.

Owing to efforts on the part of the D.A. and staff of
this Station have failed to obtain any evidence to support
a prosecution under S.D... Police that the two songs
"Daa Haa Kiang" and the drama "Ba Se Dong" are occasionally
surreptitiously rendered in Chinese low class cabarets in
the Settlement.

D. __________

Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch)

S1 Answer
8x12    S3 (b. D. I. Munce,
26/1    Could you do anything to
        keep S2?
        [Signature]

S2
Please
verify. If
correct I will
add file to
D.O. "A"
JMS

We have no Chinese Detective attached to
L3. Therefore it is difficult for us to follow up the above matter
my latest information is that the music of the song "Da Haa-
Kiang" is played in Chinese Cabarets, Dancing Halls
in the Lun Shan, Shanghai, and Chai Loh Hotels in Lower
District. This matter might be dealt with by the S.D.A. own people.

我获得的最新消息是，歌曲《Da Haa-Kiang》的乐曲在下区

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
File No. **〔此处转录不清〕**
Section 2, Special Branch,
REPORT
Date December 31, 1934.

Subject (in full) Ban on "Hula Hula Dance", the song "Dau Hua Kiang" and
the drama "Ba Sz Doong" by Bureau of Education.

Made by D.I. Everest. Forwarded by **〔此处转录不清〕**

The statement made in the Chen Pao and other local Chinese
newspapers on December 12, 1934, to the effect that the Bureau
of Education had issued a circular order forbidding the
performance of the "Hula Hula Dance," the song "Dau Hua Kiang,"
and the drama "Ba Sz Doong" has been verified.

In the case of Chinese cabarets in the Settlement the order
was conveyed by letter from the Social Bureau of the Shanghai
City Government.

Observations made by C.D.S. 48 at various times during the
past three weeks show that local Chinese places of entertain-
ment are observing the order.

**〔此处转录不清〕**

D. I. Everest.
D. I.

Deputy Commissioner (Special Branch)

S 3,
Are the forbidden displays being
given at any foreign places of entertainment?
J.H.G.

（左侧边栏批注：）
$2 (D.I. Everest)
Please
endeavour
to obtain
evidence
with a view
to prosecution
and report.
See "A".
JHG
A 1935
SBR 4/1.
A

Sir,
The Hula Hula Dance, a Hawaiian
entertainment; occasionally appears in foreign Cinema
films which so far have been passed by the Municipal Film
Censorship Board. This dance is seldom performed in the
local theatres. The Chinese song "Da Hua Xiang" (Flowery River),
and a drama entitled "Ri-zig-bong" "Bewildering Hole" are
not adapted to foreign theatres, but are occasionally
 surreptitiously rendered in Chinese low-class cabarets
in the Settlement.
**〔此处转录不清〕** 31/12.

上海公共租界工部局警务处。
档案号 **〔此处转录不清〕**
特务科第二股，
报告
日期：1934年12月31日。

主题（全称）教育局禁止“胡拉胡拉舞”、歌曲《Dau Hua Kiang》及
戏剧《Ba Sz Doong》。

由警督 Everest 呈报。转呈者 **〔此处转录不清〕**

经核实，1934年12月12日《申报》及其他本地中文报纸上刊登的
声明属实，该声明称教育局已发布通令，禁止表演
“胡拉胡拉舞”、歌曲《Dau Hua Kiang》及戏剧《Ba Sz Doong》。

就租界内的华人歌舞厅而言，该命令是通过上海市政府
社会局的信函传达的。

刑事侦缉股第48号在过去三周内不同时间进行的观察显示，
本地华人娱乐场所正在遵守该命令。

**〔此处转录不清〕**

警督 Everest.
警督。

副总监（特务科）

S 3，
是否有外国娱乐场所
上演被禁节目？
J.H.G.

（左侧边栏批注：）
$2 (警督 Everest)
请
设法
获取
证据
以便
起诉
并报告。
见“A”。
JHG
A 1935
SBR 4/1.
A

先生，
胡拉胡拉舞是一种夏威夷
娱乐项目；偶尔出现在外国电影
影片中，这些影片迄今已通过工部局
电影审查委员会的审查。这种舞蹈在
本地剧院很少表演。中文歌曲《Da Hua Xiang》（花江），
以及一部名为《Ri-zig-bong》“迷魂洞”的戏剧，
并不适合外国剧院，但偶尔会在
租界内的低级华人歌舞厅中秘密演出。
**〔此处转录不清〕** 12月31日。

备忘录。
警务处。
工部局。
上海，1934年12月13日。
致特务科。

请对“A”发表意见。该舞蹈
是否在租界内表演，或
这些歌曲是否在租界内演唱？

March 7, 1936.    2    Morning Translation.

Ta Mei Wan Pao (大美晚報) dated Mar. 6.

ESPIONAGE WORK IN FOKIEN PROVINCE

In view of the fact that the European and
American Powers have no time to give any attention
to affairs in the Far East, a certain country recently
attempted to make the five provinces in North China
establish a puppet organization. The monthly expenditure
for espionage work throughout the world is estimated at
over $10,000,000, of which sum several millions are spent
in China. Besides this money which is supplied directly
by the government, further sums can be derived from illegal
businesses, such as trafficking in drugs and munitions.
Take Fukien Province only. There a certain
government spends a monthly sum of $60,000 plus a further
amount of $30,000 from the illegal businesses in Amoy.
Two big espionage organs have been established: one in
Amoy and the other in Foochow. Each of the two
districts has an officer-in-charge and a senior special
affairs officer. Spies are active in South Fukien
along Chwang Loong (漳龍) up to Ting Chow (汀州), and
along the Chekiang Highway to Foo Chen (浦城). There
are nine district espionage branches in the Amoy
municipality and six district branches in the Foochow
municipality. Under the district branches, sections
are formed, and intelligence offices are organized under
the control of these sections. These intelligence
officers comprise certain nationals, Chinese traitors and
employees of various official organs who have been bought
over by these nationals. Therefore, should any
incident happen, big or small, the Consulate can quickly
have a clear understanding of the trouble and devise
ways and means to deal with it.

General Chiang Ting Wen, Fukien Pacification
Commissioner, arrived at Shanghai from Nanking en route
to Fukien. According to his followers, peace and order
in Fukien Province was recently much disturbed by a small
number of traitors who have been creating disturbances
along An Chi (安溪) and Nan Jih (南日). General
Chiang Ting Wen will leave for Fukien in a few days, as he
is anxious to put down these troubles.

China Times and other local newspapers:

BAN ON TWO CHINESE SONGS

As the songs entitled "Dau Hwa Kiang" (桃花江 Peach
Blossom River) and "Mau Mau Yu" (毛毛雨) are considered
obscene, the Education Bureau of the Shanghai City
Government some time ago placed a ban on these songs.
Upon receipt of information to the effect that the
Dau Hwa (桃花) Young Girls Singing & Dancing Group had
sung the "Dau Hwa Kiang" at the Great World Amusement
Resort (大世界), the Bureau has issued a further order
prohibiting the song and threatening severe punishment
in case of a further violation of this order.
pages.zh:
1936年3月7日。    2    晨间译文。

3月6日《大美晚报》。

福建省的间谍活动

鉴于欧美列强无暇顾及远东事务，
某国最近试图使华北五省建立傀儡组织。
估计全球间谍活动的每月支出超过
10,000,000美元，其中数百万美元花在中国。
除了政府直接提供的这笔资金外，
还可以从非法业务中获得更多资金，
例如毒品和军火走私。
仅以福建省为例。某国政府在那里
每月支出60,000美元，此外还有来自厦门
非法业务的30,000美元。
建立了两个大型间谍机构：一个在
厦门，另一个在福州。这两个
地区各有一名主管官员和一名高级特务官员。
间谍在闽南地区活跃，沿漳龙线直至汀州，
并沿浙江公路至浦城。厦门市有九个区级间谍分部，
福州市有六个区级分部。在区级分部之下设立科室，
并在这些科室的控制下组织情报办公室。
这些情报人员包括某些外籍国民、汉奸以及
被这些外籍国民收买的各官方机构雇员。因此，
无论发生大小事件，领事馆都能迅速
清楚了解事态，并 devised 应对之策。

福建省绥靖主任蒋鼎文将军从南京抵达上海，
途经前往福建。据其随从称，福建省近期的和平与秩序
受到少数汉奸的严重扰乱，他们在安溪和南日一带制造骚乱。
蒋鼎文将军急于平息这些动乱，将于数日后启程前往福建。

《字林西报》及其他本地报纸：

禁止两首中文歌曲

由于名为《Dau Hwa Kiang》（桃花江 Peach Blossom River）
和《Mau Mau Yu》（毛毛雨）的歌曲被认为淫秽，
上海市政府教育局此前已禁止这些歌曲。
在收到消息称《桃花》女子歌舞团在
大世界游乐场演唱了《Dau Hwa Kiang》后，
该局又发布了一道命令，禁止该歌曲，并威胁
若再次违反此令将予以严惩。
